Q: naming convention for class in java - all caps A:

Personally I would favour VipSelector, because when you start using that, you end up with methods like getVipSelector which map to a property name of vipSelector.

In constrast, VIPSelector ends up as getVIPSelector which becomes a property name vIPSelector... and that looks really ugly in things like XML, JSON, expression language, etc.

Q: How to aggregate non-uniform snapshot data into minute bars with session boundaries and tolerance in DolphinDB? A: 
// 1. Define the core logic in a function for re-usability
def getBarLabel(dt) {
    t = time(dt)
    // Define the right-closed bar label
    // bar(dt - 1, 1m) + 1m ensures (09:30:00, 09:31:00] -> 09:31:00
    label = temporalAdd(bar(temporalAdd(dt, -1, "ms"), 1m), 1, "m")
    label_t = time(label)
    
    return case 
        when (t > 11:30:00 and t <= 11:30:05) then temporalUpdate(label, 11:30:00.000)
        when (t > 15:00:00 and t <= 15:00:05) then temporalUpdate(label, 15:00:00.000)
        else label 
    end
}

// 2. Execute the aggregation
res = select 
    stdp(LastPrice) as StdPrice
from mock
where 
    (time(DateTime) > 09:30:00 and time(DateTime) <= 11:30:05) or 
    (time(DateTime) > 13:00:00 and time(DateTime) <= 15:00:05)
group by 
    SecurityID, 
    getBarLabel(DateTime) as BarLabel
order by 
    BarLabel

Q: Using proxy in playwright python A:

The timeout is not coming from your code. It is almost always the proxy. Your Playwright setup looks fine and the way you passed the proxy is correct. The issue is that most free proxy list servers barely work, go down often, or only support plain HTTP. When Playwright tries to load an HTTPS page through one of these proxies, it usually hangs until it times out. A quick way to confirm this is to test the proxy outside of Playwright first. You can try putting it in your browser or run:

curl -x http://203.176.179.255:8080 https://grabify.link/4R47U5

If that does not load, the proxy itself is not responding. In that situation, the fix is to use a different proxy. The Python code you wrote does not need to be changed.

Q: Best way to store current date (day month and year) A:

Follow a standard outlined in ISO 8601: ISO 8601 is an international standard covering the worldwide exchange and communication of date and time-related data.

To this end, use "2026-04-23T02:06:08Z" as a string for the present moment (or possibly struct tm). It is in UTC.

Use standard <time.h> functions to convert to/from a struct tm and time_t.

As timegm() is not in C89, but C23, use various source code to replicate it. Do not use mktime(). mktime() is a rabbit hole of problems when trying to use with UTC.
